name: flexon (SIMD JSON parser)
verdict_reason: In the independent rust_serialization_benchmark run of 2026-10-05, flexon 0.4.9 deserialized 1.48x-1.93x faster than serde_json 1.0.151 on all four datasets and beat simd-json's deserialization on each. Serialization was 1.30x-1.54x faster than serde_json but behind simd-json.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark with public code; rustc 1.101.0-nightly, the CPU and LTO are stated.
claimed_speedup: Deserialize: 3.6965 ms vs 6.1963 ms (log), 53.131 ms vs 102.52 ms (mesh), 4.4470 ms vs 7.1952 ms (minecraft_savedata), 22.583 ms vs 33.502 ms (mk48); 1.48x-1.93x faster. Serialize: 2.3589 ms vs 3.6304 ms, 66.328 ms vs 86.367 ms, 2.3604 ms vs 3.5385 ms, 12.812 ms vs 19.186 ms; 1.30x-1.54x faster (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Same four datasets as the rest of rust_serialization_benchmark, round-tripped as JSON through serde derives; flexon deserializes from its NullPadded source buffer.
hardware: AMD EPYC 7763 (4-vCPU GitHub Actions runner under Hyper-V)
toolchain: rustc 1.101.0-nightly (2026-10-04), bench profile lto = true, no target-cpu flag
platforms: x86_64 (SSE2 always, AVX2 via runtime detection for skipping APIs); SWAR elsewhere; std and alloc are optional features
one_liner: Young SIMD JSON parser with serde support; an independent benchmark has it deserializing 1.5x-1.9x faster than serde_json.
how_it_is_fast: Uses hardware SIMD where available (SSE2 is always on for x86_64) and SWAR elsewhere to scan JSON. Runtime detection enables AVX2 for its unchecked field-skipping APIs. The benchmark parses from flexon's NullPadded source type, a padded input buffer.
use_it_when: Deserializing JSON into serde types where decode speed matters
Config-style JSON that needs comments, trailing commas or spans, which flexon supports as opt-in features
Extracting one value from a large document with get_from
skip_it_when: Serialization-heavy workloads: simd-json serialized faster on all four datasets
You need a long-established crate: first release 2025-10, 68 stars, 0.x API
caveats: Single source of numbers; the README's Performance section is empty
Only typed serde round trips were measured; untyped Value parsing was not
tradeoffs: Pre-1.0 crate from a single maintainer
Input goes through a padded source type in the fastest path
Comment and span support are compile-time options because they slow general parsing, per the README

evidence.quote: This data set is composed of mk48.io game updates that contain data with many exploitable patterns and invariants.
On `x86_64`, SSE2 is used regardless of this flag as it is a baseline feature.
